approval_time_estimate: Review required for public apps (timeline not published)
summary: Figma OAuth apps are created under My Apps and must belong to a team or organization. A new app is a draft that only you and plan admins can authorize; private apps can be published without review for your own team or org, while public apps need Figma's review with a description, logo and testing instructions. Authorization codes expire after 30 seconds and access tokens last 90 days.
key_facts: Create the app at figma.com/developers/apps; it must be associated with a team or organization
The client secret is shown only once
Draft apps can only authorize you and your plan admins
Private apps publish without Figma review and work for the associated team/org; public apps require review (description, logo, testing instructions)
Authorization codes expire after 30 seconds — exchange immediately
Access tokens last 90 days; Figma keeps only one access token per app per user, and refreshing invalidates the previous one
Authorization must happen in a regular browser; embedded WebViews are not supported

steps.title: Create the app
steps.description: Go to My Apps, click Create a new app, name it, and associate a team or organization. Save the client ID and secret (the secret is shown once).

steps.title: Register redirect URLs and scopes
steps.description: On the OAuth credentials page add your redirect URLs (for Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback); on the scopes page select the scopes matching the endpoints you call (e.g. file_content:read).

steps.title: Choose visibility and publish
steps.description: Private apps can be published without review for your team/org. Public apps must be submitted for Figma review with a description, logo and testing instructions.
warnings: Public apps wait on Figma review — the timeline is not published

steps.title: Authorize and exchange the code
steps.description: Send users to https://www.figma.com/oauth, then POST to https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token within 30 seconds (HTTP Basic with client ID and secret).

steps.title: Refresh tokens
steps.description: POST to https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/refresh with the refresh_token; always store the newest access token.

requirements.account_type: Figma account in a team or organization

blockers.title: Draft apps only work for you and plan admins
blockers.description: Until the app is published, other users (even teammates outside the admin group) cannot authorize it.
blockers.workaround: Publish as private for internal use, or submit as public for review.

blockers.title: Public review
blockers.description: Public apps require Figma review with a description, logo and testing instructions; no timeline is published.

blockers.title: One token per user
blockers.description: Figma keeps one access token per app per user; refreshing invalidates the previous one.
